title:
Restore live-faithful nested header markup to the Vercel sandbox capture and guard the
-to-space normalisation path
objective:
A merged slice flattened Hobby
(Included) to Hobby (Included) in the vercel-sandbox-pricing capture. That removed the only exercise of the HTML adapter's dedicated
-to-space normalisation branch anywhere in the fixture tree, and a rewritten test then PINNED the flattened form, so the coverage loss is now actively defended by an assertion. Re-derive the capture from the live page so it carries the nested markup again, repoint the assertions at the live-faithful form without weakening any control, and add a guard test that becomes UNPRODUCIBLE if the normalisation branch is removed.
measured_premise: P1 CONFIRMED 2026-08-14 on base 73f83d23: zero occurrences of '<br' and zero of '<strong' anywhere under tests/fixtures/ingest/ (101 files). Positive control on the same command in the same tree: 136 occurrences of '<th'. The zero is real, not a tooling artefact. The owner premise is CONFIRMED exactly.

P2 CONFIRMED WITH A WORDING CORRECTION, live re-fetch 2026-08-14, HTTP 200, 906122 bytes: the live page at https://vercel.com/docs/sandbox/pricing still serves nested header markup. The count of three is right but denotes three nested header CELLS, not three copies of the Hobby cell: Hobby
(Included), Pro
(Per month), Enterprise
(Per month). The whole document holds exactly 3 '' with NO space, not the '
' given in the brief; the fixture follows what the page actually serves.

P3 MEASURED: the React server-component payload later in the same document independently encodes the same structure as ["$","strong",null,{"children":"Hobby"}],["$","br",null,{}],"(Included)", corroborating the rendered HTML rather than relying on it alone.

P4 MEASURED, LIVE -> FIXTURE as PRIMARY: every one of the 8 live data rows and all 4 cells per row appear in the fixture with byte-identical values. The ONLY structural divergence between live and fixture is the header markup. No live row, cell, or value is missing from the capture.
P5 MEASURED: the live document holds 7 tables; the capture retains 1 and discloses 6 removed. That reconciles exactly with the existing capture.json trim disclosure.

P6 MEASURED from source: normspace is ' '.join(value.split()), which collapses whitespace but NEVER inserts it. The space in the profile's required header 'Hobby (Included)' therefore exists ONLY because handle_starttag appends ' ' for a
inside a cell (apps/api/app/ingest/adapters/html.py:460-462). Remove that branch and the live header normalises to 'hobby(included)', which fails the header_signature subset test and yields table_not_found.

P7 MEASURED: the coverage loss is actively defended. tests/unit/test_adapter_html_matrix.py asserts '<th>Hobby (Included)</th>' in html, which is an assertion that the fixture does NOT carry the live nested form. Repointing it is required, and is a strengthening rather than a weakening.
in_scope: tests/fixtures/ingest/vercel/html/vercel-sandbox-pricing/capture.json (refresh sha256_stored; disclose retained and stripped inline markup explicitly)
tests/unit/test_adapter_html_matrix.py (repoint the flattened-form assertions at the live nested form)
tests/unit/test_adapter_vercel.py (repair mutations that string-replace the flattened header; add the nested-header normalisation guard)
.secrets.baseline ONLY via scripts/refresh_secrets_baseline.py, and only if fixture line movement changes its digests
out_of_scope_zero_diff: apps/api/app/ingest/adapters/html.py. The normalisation path is expected to be CORRECT; this slice restores its coverage, it does not change it. If it proves defective, STOP and report instead of editing.
apps/api/app/ingest/adapters/profiles/gcp.py, tests/fixtures/ingest/gcp/**, config/examples/providers/gcp.example.yaml, docs/PROVIDER_ADAPTERS.md (a concurrent Google Cloud slice owns these)
agent-state/feature_list.json (byte-identical to base; F008 stays passes:false)
any manifest, lockfile, override, or audit configuration (the nanoid GHSA-2v37-7h3g-55p8 Dependency audit failure is an accepted, documented risk that also fails on untouched main)
promotion or merge of the draft pull request
acceptance_criteria: A1 FAITHFULNESS: the capture carries the live nested header markup verbatim for all three tier columns, spelled exactly as the live page serves it.
A2 OUTCOME EQUALITY: the restored capture extracts the same facts it does today. Every existing Vercel fact assertion passes unchanged.

A3 THE DECISIVE TEST: removing the
-to-space branch makes a SPECIFIC named failure UNPRODUCIBLE on an input that should exercise it. Not merely that some tests go red.
A4 COLLATERAL CHECK: under the same mutation a HEALTHY document still extracts normally, distinguishing 'this guard stopped firing' from 'something upstream collapsed'.
A5 UNIQUE ANCHOR: the mutation anchor matches EXACTLY ONCE, and the exact patched line is printed so the mutation is shown to be what its label claims.
A6 BYTE-EXACT RESTORE: html.py is restored byte-exactly, proved by git hash-object against git rev-parse ref:path, never numstat.
A7 NO CONTROL WEAKENED, NO TEST LOST: collected test count does not fall, and no assertion is deleted or loosened.
A8 Z0 UNREACHABLE: requires_card stays ABSENT for every Vercel candidate and the classifier returns a non-Z0 verdict blocking on unknown card status.
A9 PROTECTED STATE: feature_list.json byte-identical, F008 still passes:false, zero diff to every locked path, progress.md insertions-only.
A10: the pull request is opened as a DRAFT and is not merged.
verification_plan: Re-derive origin/main with git ls-remote before branching and again immediately before reporting.
Bootstrap the venv FIRST; a fresh worktree lacks one and missing tooling produces phantom failures that prove nothing.
Record a BEFORE full-suite pass and collected test count on the untouched tree as a positive control.
State each mutation prediction BEFORE measuring, and record where the prediction was wrong.
Perform mutations on a COPY of html.py outside the repository where possible; restore and prove restoration by blob hash.
Run any filtered git diff UNFILTERED first as a positive control.
Quote git ranges as "$base..HEAD" so PowerShell does not split at the dot.
Open a draft PR and inspect its state with gh pr view.
negative_tests:
The guard test must FAIL when the
-to-space branch is removed, and the failure must be the specific header-normalisation failure, not an unrelated collapse.
A healthy already-flat document must STILL extract under the same mutation (collateral control).
The renamed_tier mutation must still yield table_not_found after the fixture regains nested markup, proving the repaired mutation still targets what its label claims.
requires_card must never appear in a Vercel candidate; a candidate that supplied it would make Z0 reachable on no official evidence.
data_implications: No migration, no schema change, no persisted state. Test fixtures and tests only.
security_privacy: No network access is added to the product. The live page was fetched once, by hand, to re-derive a capture; the fetched artefact is kept outside the repository. No credential material is involved.
portability: Standard library only; no new dependency. The restored markup is plain HTML parsed by the existing stdlib HTMLParser path.
z0_risk: Bounded and disclosed. The normalisation path fails CLOSED: losing it yields table_not_found and the candidate is rejected, so no false free claim can ship through it. The risk this slice removes is the SECOND-ORDER one: an unguarded path that silently stops working, plus a fixture that is easier than reality and an assertion defending that gap. Vercel remains non-Z0 throughout; no official Vercel page proves no-card, so requires_card stays absent and Z0 stays UNREACHABLE.
